content: Francisco Averhoff, affiliated with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in the United States, within the Region of the Americas, reported no conflicts of interest. Graham Cooke, associated with Imperial College London in the United Kingdom, within the European Region, declared no conflicts of interest. Benjamin Cowie, representing the WHO Collaborating Centre for Viral Hepatitis at the Royal Melbourne Hospital in Australia, within the Western Pacific Region, reported no conflicts of interest. Sharon Hutchinson, from Glasgow Caledonian University in the United Kingdom, within the European Region, declared no conflicts of interest. Maria Cassia Mendes Correa, affiliated with the Ministry of Health in Brazil, within the Region of the Americas, reported no conflicts of interest. Christian Ramers, associated with the Clinton Health Access Initiative in the United States, within the Region of the Americas, disclosed financial relationships with Gilead, Merck, BMS, Janssen, and AbbVie, serving on scientific advisory boards and consulting for a total of $85,000. Additionally, he received a grant of $164,000 focused on HCV testing. These financial disclosures were interpreted in the context of potential conflicts of interest. No substantive changes were made to the review based on this information. Trevor Stratton, employed by the Canadian Aboriginal AIDS Network in Canada, within the Region of the Americas, reported an annual salary of CAD $70,000. This financial disclosure was also interpreted in the context of potential conflicts of interest. No substantive changes were made to the review based on this information.
